title: Implicit Transport Geometry and Directional Admissibility in Biparametric Pullback Spaces
content: We study the functional analytic structure of weighted pullback spaces Dwϕ defined on the open unit interval (0, 1). Rather than prescribing the underlying coordinate transport map directly, we generate it implicitly through the automatic compactification of the nonlinear parametric relation Rp + qR = ev, where p ∈ (0, 1] regulates left-endpoint algebraic compression and q ≥ 0 governs right-endpoint domain redistribution. We prove that Dwϕ is isometrically isomorphic to a classical weighted Hilbert space L2((0, 1), ρ(x) dx), explicitly constructing the two-sided inverse operator to establish surjectivity. Using an orthogonal spatial decomposition based on disjoint supports on the transport line, we isolate independent boundary integration thresholds. We derive precise directional variations of the localized energy densities with respect to continuous parameter deformations, clarifying the analytical balance between coordinate transport and weight redistribution components. Finally, we establish a global admissibility criterion for dual power-law singular profiles, verify the density of algebraic polynomials, and characterize the action of the parametric variation fields.
